name: Dijkstra shortest paths
definition: Initialize d(s)=0 and all other labels =∞. Repeatedly finalize the unsettled vertex u with minimum d(u), then relax each outgoing edge by d(v)←min(d(v),d(u)+w(u,v)). Stop when all remaining distances are infinite.
variables: s source, d tentative distance, w edge cost, u finalized vertex
assumptions: Finite graph with nonnegative edge costs
limitations: A negative edge can invalidate the finalized label
failure_conditions: A negative edge can invalidate the finalized label
computation: O((V+E) log V) with a binary heap and decrease-key
application: Find minimum-cost movement routes across a position graph assembled from earlier tracking data
required_inputs: Timestamped graph edges and an explicit interpretation of weights, or a synthetic graph.
data_rights: Use synthetic inputs or source-authorized historical records. Verify licence before acquisition.
incompatible_methods: Inputs first available after the forecast cutoff

name: Bellman–Ford shortest paths
definition: Set d₀(s)=0 and d₀(v)=∞ otherwise. For k=1,…,|V|−1, set d_k(v)=min(d_(k−1)(v), min_(u→v)(d_(k−1)(u)+w(u,v))). Further strict improvement at k=|V| detects a reachable negative cycle.
variables: k edge budget, w directed edge cost, s source vertex, V vertex set
assumptions: Finite weighted directed graph; shortest distances are finite only for reachable vertices unaffected by reachable negative cycles
limitations: A reachable negative cycle requires separate handling before returning affected distances
failure_conditions: A reachable negative cycle requires separate handling before returning affected distances
computation: O(VE) edge relaxations and O(V) working memory with two label arrays
application: Find a least-cost route in a historical tactical transition graph with signed adjustments
required_inputs: Timestamped graph edges and an explicit interpretation of weights, or a synthetic graph.
data_rights: Use synthetic inputs or source-authorized historical records. Verify licence before acquisition.

name: Floyd–Warshall all-pairs paths
definition: Start D_ij=min costs of direct i→j edges, with ∞ for missing edges and the empty path of weight 0 on the diagonal. For each k set D_ij←min(D_ij,D_ik+D_kj) for all i,j. A negative D_ii signals a negative cycle.
variables: D distance matrix, i,j endpoints, k newly allowed intermediate vertex
assumptions: Finite graph; no negative cycle for ordinary finite shortest-path interpretation
limitations: Dense working memory and cubic runtime are prohibitive on large sparse graphs
failure_conditions: Dense working memory and cubic runtime are prohibitive on large sparse graphs
application: Precompute minimum transition costs among a small set of tactical zones
required_inputs: Timestamped graph edges and an explicit interpretation of weights, or a synthetic graph.
data_rights: Use synthetic inputs or source-authorized historical records. Verify licence before acquisition.

name: Kruskal minimum spanning forest
definition: Start F=∅. Process undirected edges in nondecreasing cost order; set F←F∪{e} only when the endpoints of e belong to different components of F.
variables: F set of accepted edges, e weighted undirected edge, components maintained by union–find
assumptions: Finite undirected graph; use a stable tie-break if a reproducible forest is required
limitations: Ties can yield several optimal forests and the forest omits redundant edges relevant to robustness
failure_conditions: Ties can yield several optimal forests and the forest omits redundant edges relevant to robustness
computation: O(E log E) sorting plus near-linear union–find work
application: Summarize a graph of distances among historical team playing styles

name: HITS hub and authority scores
definition: For nonnegative adjacency A where rows are sources, seek a,h with a∝Aᵀh and h∝Aa and normalize to unit Euclidean norm. Take leading right and left singular vectors for a and h, with paired signs.
variables: A weighted adjacency, a authority vector, h hub vector
assumptions: Nonzero graph; simple largest singular value for uniqueness up to joint sign
limitations: Disconnected dominant components can tie, and small spectral gaps make scores sensitive
failure_conditions: Disconnected dominant components can tie, and small spectral gaps make scores sensitive
computation: Sparse power iteration uses two matrix–vector products per iteration
